title: Characterizing Elements with Non-Optimal XOR-Count
summary: A search found implementations with at most three additions for examined elements outside proper subfields; observed XOR-count-two cases had pentanomial minimal polynomials; characterizing non-optimal cases is open.

formal_statement.body: For nontrivial elements $\alpha\in\mathrm{GF}(2^n)$, characterize those having non-optimal XOR-count in implementations of multiplication by $\alpha$. Existing search results show that every examined $\alpha$ not contained in a proper subfield can be implemented with at most three additions, and that whenever XOR-count $2$ is attainable, the minimal polynomial of $\alpha$ is a pentanomial in all examined cases. The unresolved task is to obtain a more thorough characterization of the elements with non-optimal XOR-count.

scope.domain: Lightweight finite-field multiplication and XOR-count structure in binary extension fields.
assumptions: α is a nontrivial element of GF(2^n).
parameters: n: determines the binary extension field GF(2^n)
α: field element defining the multiplication implementation whose XOR-count is studied
scope.unresolved_remainder: Characterize more thoroughly which nontrivial α in GF(2^n) have non-optimal XOR-count in multiplication-by-α implementations.

citations.label: Lightweight Multiplication in GF(2^n) with Applications to MDS Matrices

progress.summary: The source reports search-based evidence: every examined α outside a proper subfield has an implementation using at most three additions, and every examined XOR-count-two case has a pentanomial minimal polynomial. It explicitly leaves a more thorough characterization of elements with non-optimal XOR-count as an open problem.
